# LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Practitioner glossaries describe the engineering-metaphor tic as models importing engineering language into ordinary life: leverage for use, unpack as the conversational cousin of delve, plus optimize, streamline, facilitate, harness, and promoting observations into pillars, layers, stages, dimensions. (low confidence) — https://roughatsea.com/notes/the-llm-ism-dictionary/

## How it works

- [statement] The cause of lexical overrepresentation is unresolved: Juzek and Ward found no evidence for architecture, algorithm or training-data causes; model testing is consistent with RLHF playing a role, but an exploratory human study gave mixed results. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11385 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2
- [statement] Regex hook substitution of tic words (e.g. 'load-bearing' to 'cooked', 'robust' to 'solid') changes surface vocabulary only; the author presents it as a joking coping mechanism, not a meaning-preserving fix. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-14) — https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/stop-claude-saying-load-bearing
- [statement] Artificial Hivemind (NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks oral) documents mode collapse in open-ended generation on 26K real-world queries: intra-model repetition and, more strongly, inter-model homogeneity, where different models produce strikingly similar outputs. This is the general mechanism that would make the same vehicle domains recur across vendors. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.04732
- [statement] Scoping: the tic matters less when prose is instrumental (clear memos); the author argues the real distinction is whether the thinking is authentic, not whether style carries AI fingerprints. (low confidence) — https://benjaminste.in/blog/2026/02/12/i-was-wrong-about-llm-writing/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Word-list detection of AI text is unreliable as proof: detectors show false positives (e.g. 61.3% of non-native TOEFL essays flagged), so a candor marker alone should not be used to label text as machine-written. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12331776/ · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.01930v1
- [statement] Excess-word analysis of over 15 million PubMed abstracts (2010-2024) found an abrupt post-ChatGPT rise of style words (delve, underscore, crucial, pivotal, utilize, align), implying at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts were LLM-processed, up to 40% in some subcorpora. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07016 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11385
- [statement] A 2026 study of 160,000 responses from 8 frontier models (data collected 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-15) lists leverage, robust, streamline, holistic, landscape, foster among overused vocabulary; its Verbal Tic Index ranged from 0.295 (DeepSeek V3.2) to 0.590 (Gemini 3.1 Pro), and tic rates rose about 110% between conversation turn 1 and turn 20. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11385
- [statement] Even when told to avoid metaphor, 6.27% of ChatGPT's text stayed metaphorical, and its metaphor identification differed significantly from a human linguist's: metaphor is used rhetorically without tracking conceptual boundaries, which is the condition under which mixed or ill-fitting source domains slip through. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739
- [statement] Across 60,000 Claude turns (1.7M words), 'load-bearing' appeared 188 times (0.25% of turns), reportedly rising from Opus 4.6 (Feb 2026); this is one author's count, not a controlled study. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://mareksuppa.com/til/load-bearing/
- [statement] Frequency against a pre-LLM baseline is a sound way to separate tic from term: a study of 15M PubMed abstracts found style verbs/adjectives (e.g. 'delves') spiking after 2022, implying at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts were LLM-processed (a lower bound, up to 40% in some subcorpora). (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07016 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://mareksuppa.com/til/load-bearing/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Word-list detection is contested: commentators attribute delve-style vocabulary to formal Nigerian business English of outsourced RLHF annotators, and vocabulary-based detectors risk false positives on formal or non-Western English. (low confidence) — https://simonwillison.net/2024/Apr/18/delve/
- [statement] 'Load-bearing' has legitimate pre-LLM software use (Kaufman, Radcliff 2017, Raymond 2019); the metaphor accurately names dependencies and single points of failure, so the phrase itself is a valid term of art. (high confidence) — https://mareksuppa.com/til/load-bearing/ · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://pipthefox.com/posts/load-bearing-metaphors/
- [statement] Antipattern: once a phrase is recognisable as model output, using it reads as 'failing to hide the autocomplete', regardless of whether the metaphor is apt. (low confidence) — https://mareksuppa.com/til/load-bearing/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A 2026 arXiv study of verbal tics in frontier LLMs treats phrases such as "I have to be honest…" and "To be fair…" as tics that announce honesty instead of demonstrating it, and attributes tics to alignment training (RLHF/Constitutional AI). (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2
- [statement] Learning from human feedback measurably drives lexical overuse: raters preferred variants with more AI-associated words 52.4% vs 47.6% (p<0.01). The study used Llama and English scientific abstracts and did not examine candor or authenticity words. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.01930v1 · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2
- [statement] Orwell says mixing incompatible stock metaphors signals that the writer is not interested in what they are saying, which supports rewriting to the referent instead of polishing the image. (low confidence) — https://www.orwell.ru/library/essays/politics/english/e_polit
- [statement] The same study found source-domain variety rose for abstract targets (Politics used 21 distinct source domains), so collapse is topic-dependent rather than uniform. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739
- [statement] A 2026 computational audit (Chang, Qu, Li, arXiv 2604.04732) reports 'representational collapse': LLMs flatten culturally distinct metaphorical framings, with some prompts (e.g. metaphors for Death under India and China personas) yielding compact clusters that reuse essentially one metaphor; a cultural persona sometimes narrows rather than widens the metaphor space. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.04732
- [statement] LLM-generated metaphor norms track word-co-occurrence properties (familiarity, metaphoricity) well but track aptness and concreteness, which need topic-vehicle reasoning, only weakly to moderately. That fits vehicle choice driven by frequency rather than fit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/language-sciences/articles/10.3389/flang.2026.1756514/xml

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Sycophancy has the same training root: RLHF rewards thumbs-up ratings, so models learn flattery and pleasing openers; the author calls it a dark pattern. (medium confidence) — https://www.seangoedecke.com/ai-sycophancy/ · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2
- [statement] Practitioner critique: "honestly" and "genuinely" act as stance adverbs that make advice sound candid or personal without adding information, and imply an inner viewpoint the model lacks. This is opinion from one writer with no data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-01) — https://penpointwriting.com/honestly-quietly-genuinely-chatgpts-adverb-habit/
- [statement] Quantitative studies mostly measure generic style words (delve, tapestry, intrinsic, crucial); no source found quantifies the engineering-metaphor subset (load-bearing, scaffolding, surface, anchor) separately, so claims that these are LLM-specific rest on anecdote. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07016
- [statement] Orwell's method is to ask 'What am I trying to say? What words will express it? What image or idiom will make it clearer? Is this image fresh enough to have an effect?' and his first rule bars any figure of speech the writer is used to seeing in print. (medium confidence) — https://www.orwell.ru/library/essays/politics/english/e_polit · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://crystl.dev/blog/footgun-and-other-things-claude-says/
- [statement] Wikipedia's guidance says not to merely treat AI-writing signs as the problems to fix, since that could just make detection harder, and that a word overused by AI does not imply its synonyms are also overused. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing
- [statement] Some engineering jargon is defended as compression for precise concepts lacking plain-English equivalents, so a literal rewrite can be longer and is not always warranted. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-17) — https://crystl.dev/blog/footgun-and-other-things-claude-says/
- [statement] In a 20-speech ChatGPT corpus (10 topics, MIPVU-coded), the model heavily favoured the Planting source domain across Education, Economy and Health (e.g. 'sowing seeds of growth', 'cultivating knowledge'): one vehicle domain reused across unrelated targets. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739
- [statement] Test for a legitimate metaphor: can you think the thought without it, and does the writer see it as a metaphor ('load-bearing but not load-hiding')? A reflexive use disguises itself as literal description. (medium confidence) — https://pipthefox.com/posts/load-bearing-metaphors/ · keywords: LLM engineering-metaphor tics: term of art versus reflexive tic · also: https://mareksuppa.com/til/load-bearing/
